adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Hyperventilation immediately lowers PaCO2 and raises pH. Chemical buffering follows rapidly, while renal reduction of bicarbonate reabsorption/generation requires more time and is least established shortly after onset.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: The immediate chemical-buffering options are real physiologic changes, not delayed compensations. After lead-in repair, the item asks which physiologic change is least fully established early; renal bicarbonate adaptation is uniquely delayed.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Independent reread found no authoritative basis to reverse the key and no alternative option remains defensible at the requested answer granularity.

correction_history.prior_defect: Lead-in asked for a 'compensatory response' while several distractors represented primary/immediate physiologic changes.
correction_history.repair: Lead-in changed to ask which physiologic change is least likely to be fully established at the early time point.
